sections.h2: Which Johnston County office handles my tax bill?
sections.html:
Tax Administration works out of the courthouse in Smithfield, 207 East Johnston Street, second floor. It keeps weekday hours from 8 to 5 and closes for county holidays.

Two phone numbers split the work, as the county contact page explains:

  • 919-989-5120 (Tax Collection): your bill, payment plans, wage garnishment, bank attachment and foreclosure policy. Write to P.O. Box 451, Smithfield, NC 27577.
  • 919-989-5130 (Tax Administration): listing property, valuation and relief programs. Write to P.O. Box 368, Smithfield, NC 27577.

An online portal shows bills, appraisal cards and sales. Sellers should also know about the downloads page, where the county posts a delinquent tax file and an accounts receivable file for lenders.

sections.h2: What is the Johnston County property tax rate?
sections.html:
The county rate is 0.510 per $100 of value for the 2026 tax year, down from 0.520 the year before, and the county fire protection service district adds 0.115. The county posts a chart that shows the 2026 and 2025 rates side by side.

The chart also lists Kenly at 0.650, Princeton at 0.585, Wilson's Mills at 0.500, Pine Level at 0.390, Downtown Smithfield at 0.160, the Moccasin Creek service district at 0.025 and a research and training zone at 0.080. Your parcel's taxing districts come from the county GIS, so call 919-989-5130 if the districts on your bill look wrong.

For fiscal year 2026-2027 the county reports how its budget splits: education 32 percent, public safety 23 percent, human services 18 percent, general government 12 percent, debt service 10 percent and physical development 5 percent. Those shares do not include town or district spending.

sections.h2: When does a Johnston County tax bill turn late?
sections.html:
The county mails statements in July, sets September 1 as the due date and treats January 5 as the last penalty-free day. Starting January 6 the balance gains 2 percent, then three-quarters of a percent for each month after that.

Billing follows the January 1 owner, but the paper statement goes to whoever the records show on June 30. If one arrives for a house you have sold, the county says to pass it to the buyer. Lenders pull their own data from the tax office and usually pay late in the year, so your copy is for your files only.

Owners who prefer installments can sign a payment agreement for the current year, accepted until the bill turns delinquent. Older unpaid years are not eligible. Ways to pay:

  • Phone: 888-327-7344, with the year and bill number
  • Web: the county pay taxes page
  • Post: Tax Collections, P.O. Box 451
  • In person: a locked drop box at the courthouse doors

Cars and trucks are handled apart from this. The state tag and tax system collects vehicle tax through the Division of Motor Vehicles.

sections.h2: What changed with the Johnston County revaluation?
sections.html:
Johnston County's last revaluation before the current one was in 2019, and the new values took effect January 1, 2025. They drive tax bills from the summer of 2025 until the next countywide revaluation, with exceptions such as new construction.

State law at G.S. 105-286 requires every county to reappraise at least every eight years. The county hired Pearson Appraisal Service for the work, and its own certified appraisers reviewed the results. Appraisers used aerial images, street-level images, sales data and the tax database, and they made field visits to more than 115,000 properties.

The county explains that appraised value and assessed value are the same as of the revaluation date. It also explains why an online estimate can differ from the tax office figure: automated models do not check whether a sale meets the statutory test, and the county screens sales by phone calls and visits. A foreclosure sale is analyzed carefully before it counts as market evidence, and your own purchase price may differ from market value.

You must report changes you make to a property, such as additions, demolished buildings, or fire and flood damage. Email taxoffice@johnstonnc.gov or call 919-989-5130, or note it on the January listing form.

sections.h2: Can I challenge a Johnston County value?
sections.html:
Yes, but only inside a window. For real property in the 2026 cycle the county accepted its valuation appeal form until 5:00 p.m. on April 28, 2026, and its appeals page says real property appeals open in February 2027.

Personal property follows a different clock: the form has to land at the tax office thirty days after the bill date. Individual and business personal property share one form, and both are on the county forms page.

After that review the next body is the equalization and review board, which G.S. 105-322 assigns to the commissioners by default. A last appeal to the state Property Tax Commission is possible under G.S. 105-290, filed with a copy to the assessor.

Listing carries a separate deadline. January is the listing month, and a late list adds a 10 percent penalty to the levy. Last year's improvements, untagged vehicles, boats, aircraft and business assets all go on the form, and a building permit does not count as listing.

sections.h2: Which relief programs apply in Johnston County?
sections.html:
The county applies the same three state homestead programs for 2026, and an owner picks one. File Form AV-9, available from the county forms page, and ask for the relief specialist at 919-989-5130.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: owner is 65, or permanently and totally disabled, and the owner plus spouse have combined income of $38,800 or less.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: same age or disability test, income cap of $58,200, and five years of owning and occupying the home.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: service-connected total and permanent disability, or a specially adapted housing benefit. A surviving spouse who has not remarried can also qualify.

The county wants applications in before June 1 of the tax year. Present use valuation for farm, forest and horticultural land runs separately, through Form AV-5 in the January listing month. A tract removed from that program owes the deferred tax for the current year plus three earlier years, with interest. Builders can also apply every January to exclude inventory value, for as long as three years on homes and five on commercial lots.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when I sell my Johnston County house?
sections.html:
Nothing is divided for you. The county neither splits nor prorates between parties, so the buyer and seller settle it by contract, through the broker or the closing attorney.

The real property page repeats the point from another angle: a mid-year transfer leaves the seller responsible, and any credit at closing is a private deal. If you owe earlier years, ask collections for a payoff figure ahead of closing, because G.S. 105-355 attaches the lien to the parcel from the listing date.

An unpaid account can end in foreclosure, after notices and a pre-foreclosure letter, with the file handed to a private attorney. Sales take place on the courthouse steps, usually starting around ten in the morning. The bidder puts down 5 percent. Ten days must pass before the sale is final, and an upset bid has to top the last by 5 percent or $750, whichever is larger. The owner may redeem by paying taxes, interest and costs until the court confirms the sale.

Census QuickFacts estimates the mid-2025 population at 256,448, an increase of 18.7 percent over the 2020 base. Land covers 792.02 square miles, and the county counts about 99,408 housing units.

  • Owners occupy 76.1 percent of households (2020-2024)
  • Typical owner-held home value: $305,600
  • Middle household income: $83,384
  • Rent at the middle: $1,146 per month
  • New building permits in 2025: 3,002
  • Average trip to work: 32.2 minutes

The courthouse and tax office are in Smithfield. Clayton, Selma, Benson, Four Oaks and other towns each levy their own rate in addition to the county's.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 tax rate for Johnston County?
faqs.a: The county levies 0.510 per $100 for 2026, down from 0.520 in 2025. The fire protection district adds 0.115, and each town adds its own rate.

faqs.q: When do Johnston County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: They turn delinquent after January 5. Interest begins January 6 at 2 percent for the first month, then three-quarters of a percent per month.

faqs.q: Will Johnston County divide the tax between me and the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The county bills the January 1 owner and does not prorate, so your broker or closing attorney should settle the split on the closing statement.

faqs.q: Can I spread Johnston County taxes over installments?
faqs.a: Yes, for the current year only. Return a payment agreement to collections before the bill goes delinquent, since prior-year balances are not eligible.

faqs.q: Whom do I ask about Johnston County tax relief?
faqs.a: Call 919-989-5130 and ask for a property tax relief specialist. The application is Form AV-9, due before June 1.
